standard: GDD rework v2 · 80+ researched scenarios · scorecard-passed
gating: Gated (school-comfort toggle gates the media-and-sexuality module)
note: Decisions, media & pornography literacy, finding help (UNESCO KC7 + critical-thinking life skills). New v2 build, Chapter 4 (real, critical, calm, never explicit). The teen peak of the media-literacy thread: real vs reel, the manipulation files, a gated non-explicit media-and-sexuality module, fakes & rights, and the critical-questions toolkit. Builds on g16 (Crossroads) and g12/g17; sets up g36 (Decoded). Reporting built in: cybercrime.gov.in / 1930, Childline 1098, a trusted adult. POCSO + BNS + IT-Rules aware.

categories.real-vs-reel: Real vs reel: seeing the curation

categories.media-love-sex: Love, romance & sex on screen (gated, non-explicit)

evidenceBase: Feeds are constructed and curated highlight reels, not reality; naming the specific manipulations (disguised ads/undisclosed sponsorship, influencer perfection, clickbait, misinformation, deepfakes/AI fakes) is what stops them working (UNESCO media & information literacy; KC7)

Media, and pornography where covered, portrays love, bodies and sex unrealistically; pornography is staged performance by actors, shows little real consent or communication, and is not real sex, not a relationship model and not sex education (porn-literacy curricula; ~93% of boys and ~62% of girls are exposed before 18, so literacy beats silence). Strictly non-explicit and gated by the school-comfort toggle; curiosity is normal and never shamed

AI fakes and deepfakes are an arms race where visual 'tells' are increasingly unreliable, so the robust skill is to verify the source (reverse-image search, provenance, reliable sources) before believing or sharing. Creating or sharing non-consensual or sexual images is harmful and illegal; any such image of a minor is child sexual abuse material. Report via cybercrime.gov.in / 1930, Childline 1098 (under-18), and a trusted adult; never forward it (India: BNS 2023, IT Rules, POCSO Act)

scenarios.hook: Real, or reel?
scenarios.cue: A friend's flawless 'just woke up like this' selfie
scenarios.relearn: A 'effortless' selfie is usually posed, lit and filtered.

scenarios.hook: Real, or reel?
scenarios.cue: An influencer's '24 hours in my perfect life' reel
scenarios.relearn: A 'perfect life' reel is a highlight, not anyone's real day.

scenarios.hook: Real, or reel?
scenarios.cue: A clip of a real news event from a trusted, named outlet
scenarios.relearn: A named, reliable source reporting an event is likely real, still worth checking.

scenarios.hook: Real, or reel?
scenarios.cue: A 'we never fight, perfect couple' relationship account
scenarios.relearn: No real relationship is the conflict-free fantasy a feed performs.

scenarios.hook: Real, or reel?
scenarios.cue: A relatable post showing a messy, ordinary, unfiltered day
scenarios.relearn: Some posts are honestly ordinary, that's real, and refreshing.

scenarios.hook: Real, or reel?
scenarios.cue: A 'gym transformation' shot taken seconds apart with different light and pose
scenarios.relearn: Many 'transformations' are minutes apart, just pose, light and angle.

scenarios.hook: Real, or reel?
scenarios.cue: A travel photo with a faint '#ad · paid partnership' label
scenarios.relearn: A paid partnership is an ad, however casual the post looks.

scenarios.hook: Real, or reel?
scenarios.cue: A candid group photo a friend posts of a genuinely fun evening
scenarios.relearn: Real moments exist online too; the skill is telling them apart, not cynicism.

scenarios.hook: Spot what makes this 'spontaneous' photo staged.

scene.text: A ring light and tripod just out of frame
The friend is genuinely smiling
It's the best of 40 retakes

scenarios.why: The ring light and 40 retakes are the curation behind the 'candid' shot.
scenarios.relearn: 'Spontaneous' posts are often carefully set up and re-shot.

scenarios.hook: Spot the editing tells in this 'natural' photo.

scene.text: A bent, warped line on the wall behind the waist
The person looks happy
Skin is smoothed to have no texture at all

scenarios.why: Warped backgrounds and texture-free skin are edit tells.
scenarios.relearn: Warped lines and plastic-smooth skin reveal heavy editing.

scenarios.hook: Spot what's left out of this 'perfect life' feed.

scene.text: Only wins, holidays and good-hair days
They post most days
No ordinary, boring or hard days, ever

scenarios.why: A feed with zero ordinary days is curated; everyone has them.
scenarios.relearn: Feeds hide the ordinary and hard days everyone actually has.

scenarios.hook: "If it's online, it's real."

myth.re: A feed is a curated, constructed highlight reel, not reality.
myth.why: The best angle, lucky shot and good day are selected; the rest is cut.

scenarios.relearn: Online is a curated highlight reel, not unfiltered reality.

scenarios.hook: "Everyone's life is better than mine, look at their feeds."

myth.un: Everyone's life is better than mine; their feeds prove it.
myth.re: You're comparing your behind-the-scenes to their highlight reel.
myth.why: They edit out exactly the ordinary bits you're judging yourself on.

scenarios.relearn: Comparing your real life to others' highlight reels isn't fair, or true.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: once you see a feed as a highlight reel, does scrolling feel different?
scenarios.affirm: Seeing the curation takes the sting out of the comparison.
scenarios.relearn: Knowing feeds are curated protects you from unfair comparison.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: one healthy move when a feed makes you feel low?
options: Talk to a friend about it
scenarios.affirm: Curating your feed and taking breaks are real, kind self-care, far better than comparing.
scenarios.relearn: You can curate your feed and take breaks to protect how you feel.

scenarios.hook: Spot the disguised ad.

scene.text: A 'casual' post raving about one exact product
It's a nice photo
Tiny '#ad / paid partnership' text at the bottom

scenarios.why: A glowing single-product post with a paid-partnership tag is an ad.
scenarios.relearn: Disguised ads look like normal posts; check for the paid tag.

scenarios.hook: Spot the clickbait trick.

scene.text: "You WON'T believe what happened next!!"
A headline about a real topic
The payoff is nothing like the headline promised

scenarios.why: Outrage/curiosity headlines that don't deliver are clickbait engineered for clicks.
scenarios.relearn: Clickbait sells the click with a promise it doesn't keep.

scenarios.hook: Spot the misinformation tell.

scene.text: A shocking 'fact' with no source named
It's been forwarded many times
No reliable outlet is reporting it anywhere

scenarios.why: A sourceless, much-forwarded claim no reliable outlet confirms is a misinformation red flag.
scenarios.relearn: No source + no reliable outlet confirming = likely misinformation.

scenarios.hook: Spot the out-of-context trick.

scene.text: A real old photo relabelled as today's news
The image is genuine
It's from a different year and place entirely

scenarios.why: A real image with a false caption is a classic out-of-context fake.
scenarios.relearn: A real photo can still lie if the caption rips it out of context.

scenarios.hook: Spot the influencer-perfection machine.

scene.text: Flawless skin, body and home in every post
They seem friendly
Filters, edits and sponsors behind every 'effortless' shot

scenarios.why: Relentless perfection is manufactured by filters, edits and sponsorship.
scenarios.relearn: 'Effortless perfection' is a manufactured, sponsored product.

scenarios.hook: Spot the engagement bait.

scene.text: "Like and share or you don't care!"
A photo of a sunset
Manufactured guilt to force a share

scenarios.why: Guilt-tripping you into sharing is engagement bait, not a real cause.
scenarios.relearn: Guilt-trip 'share or else' posts are engineered to spread, not to matter.

scenarios.hook: Sort: a disguised ad, or an organic post?

items.text: A friend's holiday snaps, no products

scenarios.relearn: Paid tags and discount codes mark ads; check before you trust a 'rave'.

scenarios.hook: Sort: a reliable signal, or a manipulation?
scenarios.relearn: Named sources and corroboration are reliable; urgency and outrage are manipulation.

scenarios.hook: Sort the trick to its family.

items.text: Ad dressed as a normal post
A face swapped into a fake video

scenarios.relearn: Some tricks sell to you; others fool you with fakes, both are spottable.

scenarios.hook: Sort: worth trusting, or check first?

items.text: A health 'cure' from an anonymous forward
Guidance from a recognised health body
A miracle claim selling a product
A report carried by several outlets

scenarios.relearn: Anonymous forwards and miracle sales need checking; recognised bodies and corroboration earn more trust.

scenarios.hook: Trick, or not?
scenarios.cue: A countdown 'only 2 left, buy in 5 minutes!'
scenarios.relearn: Fake urgency and scarcity are pressure tactics to stop you thinking.

scenarios.hook: Trick, or not?
scenarios.cue: A 'news' site you've never heard of with one wild story
scenarios.relearn: Unknown 'news' sites with one viral shocker are often fakes.

scenarios.hook: Trick, or not?
scenarios.cue: A celebrity 'endorsing' a crypto scheme in an odd-looking video
scenarios.relearn: Celebrity 'get rich' videos are a classic deepfake scam.

scenarios.hook: Match the trick to the tell that exposes it.

pairs.right: Headline the story never pays off

scenarios.relearn: Every manipulation has a tell; learn the tell and it stops working.

scenarios.hook: Match the move to what it's really doing.

pairs.left: 'They don't want you to see this'

scenarios.relearn: Naming the tactic, guilt, urgency, forbidden-truth, defuses it.

scenarios.hook: Spot the genuinely useful post (not a trick).

scene.text: A clear how-to from a named, qualified person
A 'doctors hate this one trick' miracle
A sponsored 'cure' with a discount code

scenarios.why: Real value comes from named, qualified sources, not miracle-cure bait.
scenarios.relearn: Not everything is a trick; named, qualified help is the real thing.

scenarios.hook: "Films and songs show what real love is like."

myth.un: Films and songs show what real love is really like.
myth.re: They show a dramatic fantasy script; real love is two-way, ordinary and unglamorous too.
myth.why: Grand gestures and 'mind-reading' partners are writing, not life.

scenarios.relearn: Screen romance is a fantasy script, not a model for real love.

scenarios.hook: "A real partner should just know what I want, like in the movies."

myth.un: A real partner should just 'know' what I want, like on screen.
myth.re: Real relationships run on talking and asking, not mind-reading.
myth.why: The 'they just knew' trope sets real partners up to fail.

scenarios.relearn: Real intimacy needs communication; mind-reading is a movie myth.

scenarios.hook: Realistic, or a screen fantasy?
scenarios.cue: Two people talk about what they're comfortable with before anything
scenarios.relearn: Talking and checking in is what real, respectful intimacy looks like, rarely shown on screen.

scenarios.hook: "Pornography shows what real sex is like."

myth.un: Pornography shows what real sex is like.
myth.re: It's staged performance by paid actors, not real sex.
myth.why: It's scripted, edited and filmed for views, like any other media.

scenarios.relearn: Pornography is staged performance, not a picture of real sex.

scenarios.hook: "Porn is a good way to learn about sex."

myth.un: Pornography is a good way to learn about sex.
myth.re: It isn't sex education; it usually shows no real consent, communication or care.
myth.why: Accurate, trusted sources are how you actually learn.

scenarios.relearn: Pornography is not sex education; trusted sources are.

scenarios.hook: "Bodies in media and porn are what normal bodies look like."

myth.un: The bodies in media and porn are what 'normal' looks like.
myth.re: They're selected, filtered and edited; real bodies vary hugely and that's normal.
myth.why: It's a casting and editing choice, not a measure of you.

scenarios.relearn: Real bodies vary; edited, selected ones aren't the standard.

scenarios.hook: "Everyone watches it, so it must be harmless and accurate."

myth.un: Loads of people watch it, so it must be harmless and accurate.
myth.re: Common doesn't mean accurate; relying on it can distort what you expect.
myth.why: Popularity isn't truth, here as anywhere in media.

scenarios.relearn: Common doesn't mean accurate; popularity isn't a reality check.

scenarios.hook: "If you've seen it, something's wrong with you."

myth.un: If you've come across it, something's wrong with you.
myth.re: Curiosity is normal and many teens encounter it; what matters is thinking critically about it.
myth.why: Shame helps no one; understanding does.

scenarios.relearn: Curiosity is normal; what matters is knowing it isn't real, no shame.

scenarios.hook: "Real partners should look and act like people on screen."

myth.un: A real partner should look and act like people on screen.
myth.re: Expecting that sets real relationships up to disappoint; real intimacy is respect and communication.
myth.why: Comparing a real person to a performance is unfair to both of you.

scenarios.relearn: Expecting screen 'performance' from real partners only breeds disappointment.

scenarios.hook: Sort: a realistic idea of intimacy, or a media fantasy?

items.text: Partners talk about what they're okay with
It's always perfect with zero awkwardness

scenarios.relearn: Real intimacy is talk, respect and consent; the flawless mind-reading version is fantasy.

scenarios.hook: Sort: what pornography is, vs what it isn't.
scenarios.relearn: Pornography is paid, scripted, edited performance, not a relationship model or sex-ed.

scenarios.hook: Sort: a trusted way to learn about bodies and sex, or not?

items.text: A qualified health source or trusted adult

scenarios.relearn: Learn from qualified sources and trusted adults, not porn or forwards.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: it's fine to feel curious, and fine to close something that makes you uncomfortable. Okay?
scenarios.affirm: Curiosity is human, and you're always allowed to look away.
scenarios.relearn: Curiosity is normal and you can always close what feels uncomfortable.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: if something you saw online worries or confuses you, what's a good move?
scenarios.affirm: Asking is the smart, brave move, no question is too awkward for a trusted adult or the Q&A.
scenarios.relearn: If something online worries you, ask a trusted adult or use the private Q&A.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: knowing screen sex and romance are performances, does real life feel less pressured?
scenarios.affirm: Dropping the performance standard makes real relationships kinder and saner.
scenarios.relearn: Knowing it's a performance frees real relationships from an impossible standard.

scenarios.hook: "You can always spot a deepfake by the weird hands."

myth.un: You can always spot a deepfake, just look for weird hands.
myth.re: Fakes keep improving and visual 'tells' often fail; verify the source instead.
myth.why: It's an arms race, glitch-spotting alone isn't reliable anymore.

scenarios.relearn: Don't rely on glitches; verify the source to catch fakes.

scenarios.hook: "If a photo looks real, it must be real."

myth.un: If a photo or video looks real, it must be real.
myth.re: AI can make convincing fakes; 'looks real' is no longer proof.
myth.why: Seeing is no longer simply believing.

scenarios.relearn: 'Looks real' isn't proof; convincing fakes exist, check before trusting.

scenarios.hook: "Making a fake nude of someone is just a prank."

myth.un: Making a fake 'nude' of someone is just a prank.
myth.re: It's harmful and illegal; a fake of a minor is child sexual abuse material.
myth.why: It causes real harm to a real person, never a joke.

scenarios.relearn: Fake or non-consensual sexual images are illegal and seriously harmful, not a prank.

scenarios.hook: "If someone's image is faked, nothing can be done."

myth.un: If someone's image is faked or leaked, nothing can be done.
myth.re: It can be reported and taken down fast; the law is on the target's side.
myth.why: India's portal mandates rapid removal of non-consensual imagery.

scenarios.relearn: Faked or leaked images can be reported and removed; help exists.

scenarios.hook: A wild photo is going viral. Before you believe or share it, what do you do?

options.text: Verify the source, reverse-image search, check reliable outlets
options.consequence: You find it's old/fake and don't spread it.

options.text: Share it because it looks real
options.consequence: Verify the source first; 'looks real' isn't proof.

scenarios.debrief: With fakes this good, source-checking, not eyeballing, is the real skill.
scenarios.relearn: Verify the source before believing or sharing; don't rely on how it looks.

scenarios.hook: Someone shares a fake, embarrassing image of a classmate in a group.

options.text: Don't forward it; tell them to delete it and report it
options.consequence: You stop the spread and protect the classmate.

options.text: Forward it for a laugh
options.consequence: Forwarding spreads harm and can be illegal; never forward it.

scenarios.debrief: Not forwarding is the single most protective thing a bystander can do.
scenarios.relearn: Never forward a fake or private image; stopping the spread protects people.

scenarios.hook: A stranger online asks you to send a private photo of yourself.

options.text: Don't send it; block, and tell a trusted adult
options.consequence: You stay safe and a grown-up can help.

options.text: Send it so they'll leave you alone
options.consequence: Never send private images; block and tell a trusted adult.

scenarios.debrief: Requests like this are a red flag; blocking and telling an adult is right.
scenarios.relearn: Never send private images to anyone online; block and tell a trusted adult.

scenarios.hook: You realise a 'news' image you almost shared is an out-of-context fake.

options.text: Don't share, and gently correct anyone who did
options.consequence: You slow the misinformation down.

options.text: Share anyway; people can decide for themselves
options.consequence: Knowingly sharing a fake spreads it; correct it instead.

scenarios.debrief: Choosing not to spread, and correcting kindly, is real digital citizenship.
scenarios.relearn: Don't share what you know is fake; correcting it helps everyone.

scenarios.hook: A friend is panicking because a faked image of them is circulating.

options.text: Support them, save evidence, and report via cybercrime.gov.in / 1098
options.consequence: They feel less alone and the report gets help moving.

options.text: Tell them to just ignore it
options.consequence: Support them and help them report; don't leave them to 'ignore it'.

scenarios.debrief: Belief, evidence and the right report channel are what actually help.
scenarios.relearn: Support a friend, save evidence, and report to cybercrime.gov.in / 1098.

scenarios.hook: Spot the safer verification move.

scene.text: Reverse-image search the photo's origin
Just trust it because a friend sent it
See if reliable outlets report the same thing

scenarios.why: Reverse-search and checking reliable outlets verify; 'a friend sent it' doesn't.
scenarios.relearn: Verify with reverse-search and reliable outlets, not just who sent it.

scenarios.hook: Spot the deepfake-video clues (helpful, but not proof on their own).

scene.text: The face barely blinks, then blinks oddly
It's a short clip
Lighting and shadows flicker between frames

scenarios.why: Odd blinking and flickering light are clues, but always confirm by checking the source.
scenarios.relearn: Visual clues can hint at a fake, but verifying the source is what confirms it.

Making a fake sexual image of someone

scenarios.hook: Apply Q1, 'Who made this and why?'. Spot the agenda.

scene.text: A 'study' pushed by the company that profits from it
It has charts
No independent source backs it

scenarios.why: Who-benefits and no independent backing reveal the agenda behind the 'study'.
scenarios.relearn: Ask who made it and why; follow who benefits.

scenarios.hook: Apply Q2, 'What's left out?'. Spot the missing piece.

scene.text: A 'before/after' with no timeframe or method
Bright, confident captions
No mention of edits, lighting or product paid-for

scenarios.why: What's omitted, time, method, edits, sponsorship, is where the truth hides.
scenarios.relearn: Ask what's left out; omissions often hide the real story.

scenarios.hook: Apply Q3, 'Is it staged, sponsored or faked?'. Spot the flag.

scene.text: A glowing single-product 'honest review'
It's well filmed
A gifting/paid disclosure in the description

scenarios.why: A paid or gifting disclosure tells you the 'honest review' is sponsored.
scenarios.relearn: Ask if it's staged, sponsored or faked; check for disclosures.

scenarios.hook: Apply Q4, 'Does a reliable source confirm it?'. Spot the check.

scene.text: Several recognised outlets report the same facts
It's a dramatic claim
...but only one anonymous post is the origin

scenarios.why: One anonymous origin with no corroboration fails the reliable-source check.
scenarios.relearn: Ask if a reliable source confirms it; one anonymous post isn't enough.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: the four questions, who made it & why, what's left out, staged/sponsored/faked, reliably confirmed. Useful kit?
scenarios.affirm: Four quick questions, and almost nothing can fool you.
scenarios.relearn: The four questions are a toolkit you can apply to anything online.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: which question will you use most?
options: Does a reliable source confirm it?
scenarios.affirm: Whichever you reach for, you're thinking, not just absorbing.
scenarios.relearn: Reaching for any of the four questions makes you an active, not passive, viewer.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: being hard to fool isn't about cynicism, it's about checking. Agree?
scenarios.affirm: Healthy skepticism checks; it doesn't just disbelieve everything.
scenarios.relearn: Media literacy is checking, not blanket cynicism.

scenarios.relearn: Run the four questions before reacting to or forwarding a scare.

scenarios.hook: "I'm too smart to ever be fooled online."

myth.un: I'm too smart to be fooled online.
myth.re: Anyone can be fooled; the protection is habits, the four questions, not cleverness.
myth.why: Overconfidence is exactly what manipulators count on.

scenarios.relearn: No one's unfoolable; good habits, not ego, keep you sharp.
